items.title: Brass chorister · A

versions.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. New Breachline card painting: BRASS CHORISTER, design A. Invent a substantial nonhumanoid Artificer construct, chest-high to a human but with heavy credible mass. Its body is a broad squat cast-brass resonating vessel, part bell and part ribbed working machine, carried on THREE short stout articulated supports with splayed iron shoes. A compact offset folded-metal hood forms a characterful head, a dark slit beneath its brow; no human face or futuristic robot head. One broad jointed bracing arm ends in a thick blunt paddle; a smaller tucked manipulator is optional. Distinct articulated load paths, a few exposed rods and hinges, deliberate open spaces; functional rather than gear-encrusted. It could readily shove a person aside through physical weight, but show no victim or ability demonstration. It pauses in the doorway of an Artificer's stone-and-timber workshop, one shoe raised over the worn sill, its heavy body's slight tilt giving personality. Three-quarter side view, low eye level, prominent silhouette. A large shaded workshop mass behind, copper light reflected from the brass into the floor, cool soft daylight from the doorway organizing the whole scene. Sparse tools are soft shapes. Bare brass and soot-dark iron, minimal enamel and ornament; no repeated emblems. New design proposal, not a biological creature. Traditional oil and acrylic fantasy painting with beautiful economical painted form. Build the picture from broad colour masses and deliberately varied strokes, with a few sharper accents at the focal feature. Background architecture and secondary objects are suggested in a handful of low-contrast shapes. Brush size, edge softness and detail agree locally; do not enumerate bolts, paving stones, fibres or scratches. Matte wood, stone and skin; selectively bright reflections on worked metal. No photorealism, polished 3D appearance, pore noise, uniformly crisp texture, text, letters, logo, border or watermark. Landscape 1536x1024, one coherent light source and readable forms.

Use case: stylized-concept. Create a fresh Breachline BRASS CHORISTER construct, design A. The attached accepted Dock tally-keeper sheet is a REQUIRED REFERENCE FOR MECHANICAL CONSTRUCTION: hammered worked-brass shells, riveted open ribs, shaped struts, pinned rotating joints, visible negative spaces and a simple articulated worked-metal head. Carry that established material and joint vocabulary into a NEW, MUCH STOCKIER practical construct, not the same tall thin individual. About human height, broad oval ribbed torso with a protected dark translucent core, close overlapping curved brass shoulder covers, two sturdy jointed arms with broad articulated metal hands, two strong shortened legs and wide iron-soled feet. Weight through a low centre of mass, plausible rod and joint attachments; substantial enough to shove a person, but not a giant. A short subtle mouth opening in a small hammered head, no human face and no futuristic helmet. A few small blue enamel inset panels may show ordinary Artificer craft. Use attachment 1 as required anatomy: heavy brow, broad blunt nose, strongly projecting jaw and irregular tusks; a visibly nonhuman face with one blunted tusk and a pale old scar, thinning coarse grey hair, deliberate unreadable eyes. This is not a handsome human painted green. Waist-to-knees portrait with the figure slightly left of centre; two followers dissolve into broad subdued camp shapes behind. His salvaged iron cuirass fits his torso, one modest shoulder plate and a repaired leather sleeve on the other side. Attachment 2 LEFT COLUMN informs practical salvaged construction only: radically reduce its shoulder bulk and use a normal-sized iron war hammer, with a head only about the size of his fist and a sturdy waist-high wooden haft. He rests one hand naturally around that haft; the other relaxed beside his belt. One single clear three-spike mark on a small weathered breast cloth identifies the Warhorde; nothing repeated across gear or tents. No grand throne, huge pauldrons, enormous hammer, ornamental skulls or familiar franchise design. Soft late-afternoon side light carves his broad matte face and catches a few worn iron edges, subdued umber camp canvas and moss-grey ground, no required red scheme. His stillness and the attention of the loosely suggested followers carry the power. Traditional oil-and-acrylic fantasy painting, emphatically painted through larger interlocking colour shapes and varied visible strokes. Selective crispness at face, hands and important contacts; quieter secondary edges, low-detail backgrounds built in broad masses. Skin is matte simplified form, not polished or pore-textured.
